messages.subject: {Disarmed} Reanalysis of your sheep data
parts:
Graham

In the cold light of day, I have entered your data and performed a more thorough distance sampling analysis, rather than concentrating only upon the perpendicular distances.

Note I also changed the size of the study area to 1 km^2, simply to make the values of abundance larger, I did not perform truncation, which I would likely do in a more complete analysis.  The field named "object" is extraneous and I have removed it.  It would be sequential numbering of detections, so not needed for the transects on which no detections were made.

In any event, I include my code:

library(Distance)

setwd("C:/Users/erexs/OneDrive/Desktop")

sheep <- read.csv(file="upton2.txt",header=FALSE,

                  colClasses=c("factor", "integer", "integer",

                               "numeric", "integer",

                               "numeric"))

names(sheep) <- c("Region.Label", "Area",

                  "Sample.Label", "Effort",  

                  "size", "distance")


estimate.with.size <- ds(sheep)

size.drop <- sheep

size.drop$size <- NULL

estimate.without.size <- ds(size.drop)


summary(estimate.with.size)

summary(estimate.without.size)
And the result.  Note that when "size" is present in the data, the summary produces a "summary for clusters" as well as a "summary for individuals", whereas when "size" is not present, the unlabelled summary is for individuals as group size is not referenced.

Contrast the estimates I have highlighted in red noting the effect of mean group size of 4.4.  This analysis does not incorporate an adjustment for size bias, wherein average size of detected groups is an overestimate of average size of groups in the population.  That would be accommodated by including group size as a covariate in the detection function.  Let me know if you have other questions.
